answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its account is caught coordinating fraudulent trades, while limiting influence to verified stake rather than account count. A Sybil attacker must lock real capital for every persona, so creating thousands of cheap identities no longer multiplies voting power; detection and slashing make the voyage costly. The pigment of an account profile and a tiny delta in its behavior are not proof of uniqueness, so the defense rests on scarce collateral and enforceable penalties.
